Field.name: InputFile
Field.usage: Input image file
Field.tooltip: Input image file.
Field.manpage: Input image file. This may also be entered after all arguments on the command line.

Field.name: OutputFile
Field.usage: Output image file
Field.tooltip: Output image file. If no output file is specified and the program is not run in trial mode, pixels will be replaced in the input file. USE REPLACEMENT OPTION WITH CAUTION.
Field.manpage: Output image file. This may also be entered after an input file name on the command line. If no output file is specified and the program is not run in trial mode, pixels will be replaced in the input file. USE REPLACEMENT OPTION WITH CAUTION.

Field.name: HalfFloatModeOutput
Field.usage: 1 to output 16-bit floats if input is floats, 2 to do so unconditionally
Field.manpage: Enter 2 to set the mode for output files to half-floats (16-bit floats) unconditionally, or 1 to do so only when the input file is floating point.

Field.name: PieceListFile
Field.usage: File with piece coordinates for a montaged image file
Field.tooltip: Input image file.
Field.manpage: File with piece coordinates for a montaged image file. With this entry, the program will assume that an input model was drawn on a display of the montage with overlaps adjusted to be either 0,0 or the amount indicated by the -overlaps option. The output model file with points found will also be formatted to fit on such a display.

Field.name: OverlapsForModel
Field.usage: Overlaps in X and Y at which montaged image is being viewed (default 0,0)
Field.manpage: Overlaps in X and Y at which a montaged image is being viewed both when producing an input model and viewing the output model of pixels being replaced. The same values should be used as are provided to the -o option of 3dmod. The default is 0,0, which represents no overlap between images.

Field.name: FindPeaks
Field.usage: Find peaks a criterion # of SDs above or below background
Field.tooltip: Find and erase peaks a criterion # of SDs above or below background. This option must be included for automatic removal of X-rays.
Field.manpage: Find and erase peaks a criterion # of SDs above or below background. This option must be included for automatic removal of X-rays.

Field.name: PeakCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion # of SDs above local mean for erasing peak
Field.tooltip: Criterion # of SDs above local mean for erasing peak based on intensity (the default is %{default} SDs).
Field.manpage: Criterion # of SDs above local mean for erasing peak based on intensity (the default is %{default} SDs).

Field.name: DiffCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion # of SDs above mean pixel-to-pixel difference
Field.tooltip: Criterion # of SDs above mean pixel-to-pixel difference for erasing a peak based on differences (the default is %{default} SDs).
Field.manpage: Criterion # of SDs above mean pixel-to-pixel difference for erasing a peak based on differences (the default is %{default} SDs)

Field.name: GrowCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion # of SDs above mean for adding points to peak
Field.tooltip: Criterion # of SDs above mean for adding points to peak (the default is %{default} SDs).
Field.manpage: Criterion # of SDs above mean for adding points to peak (the default is %{default} SDs).

Field.name: ScanCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion # of SDs for picking peaks in initial scan
Field.tooltip: Criterion # of SDs of mean of scan area for picking peaks in initial scan (the default is 3 SDs).
Field.manpage: Criterion # of SDs of mean of scan area for picking peaks in initial scan (the default is %{default} SDs).

Field.name: MaximumRadius
Field.usage: Maximum radius of peak area to erase
Field.tooltip: Maximum radius of peak area to erase (the default is 2.1 pixels).
Field.manpage: Maximum radius of peak area to erase (the default is %{default} pixels).

Field.name: GiantCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion # of SDs above local mean for erasing extra-large peak
Field.tooltip: Criterion # of SDs above local mean for erasing extra-large peak based on intensity (the default is 12 SDs).
Field.manpage: Criterion # of SDs above local mean for erasing extra-large peak based on intensity (the default is %{default} SDs). Enter 0 to disable this second stage of peak removal.

Field.name: ExtraLargeRadius
Field.usage: Maximum radius of extra-large peak area to erase (default %{default})
Field.tooltip: Maximum radius of extra-large peak area to erase (the default is 8 pixels).
Field.manpage: Maximum radius of extra-large peak area to erase (the default is %{default} pixels).

Field.name: BigDiffCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion for whether extra-large peak has big enough interpixel differences
Field.tooltip: Criterion for whether an extra-large peak has big enough interpixel differences to qualify for removal (the default is 19 SDs).
Field.manpage: An extra-large peak will be erased only if the value for the maximum difference between adjacent pixels, averaged over the most extreme one-fourth of the pixels in the patch, exceeds this criterion, evaluated as the number of SDs above the mean absolute difference between adjacent pixels in the scan area. The default is %{default}. This high a value is needed to prevent gold erasure on low-noise data sets with small gold particles, and a lower value may be needed to make extra-large peak removal useful.

Field.name: MaxPixelsInDiffPatch
Field.usage: Maximum number of pixels in a patch that exceeds the difference criterion
Field.tooltip: Maximum number of pixels in a patch that exceeds the difference criterion. Larger patches will not be replaced. The default is 2.
Field.manpage: Maximum number of pixels in a patch that exceeds the difference criterion. If the number of pixels that satisfy the criteria exceed this limit, none of the pixels in the patch will be replaced. The default is %{default}.

Field.name: OuterRadius
Field.usage: Outer radius of annulus to calculate local mean and SD in
Field.manpage: Outer radius of annulus around a peak in which to calculate local mean and SD (the default is 4.1 pixels). This option and -width are mutually exclusive.

Field.name: AnnulusWidth
Field.usage: Width (outer - inner radius) of annulus to calculate local mean and SD in
Field.tooltip: Width of the annulus around a peak in which to calculate local mean and SD (the default is 2.0 pixels).
Field.manpage: Difference between outer and inner radius of the annulus around a peak in which to calculate local mean and SD (the default is %{default} pixels). This option and -radius are mutually exclusive.

Field.name: XYScanSize
Field.usage: Size of regions to compute mean and SD in for initial scans
Field.tooltip: Size of regions to compute mean and SD in for initial scans (the default is 100 pixels).
Field.manpage: Size of regions to compute mean and SD in for initial scans (the default is %{default} pixels).

Field.name: EdgeExclusionWidth
Field.usage: Width of area to exclude on all edges of image
Field.tooltip: Width of area to exclude on all edges of image in pixels (default 0).
Field.manpage: Width of area to exclude on all edges of image in pixels (default %{default}).

Field.name: SearchIterations
Field.usage: Number of times to iterate search for peaks
Field.tooltip: Number of times to iterate search for peaks (default 3).
Field.manpage: Number of times to iterate search for peaks. For a given section, the iterations will be terminated after an iteration with no changes. Moreover, the program will keep track of which scan regions have changes on each iteration and stop redoing regions that have had no changes. The default is %{default}.

Field.name: PointModel
Field.usage: Output model file with points replaced in peak search
Field.manpage: Output model file with points replaced in peak search. Each patch of points will be in a separate contour. Patches are sorted into separate objects based on how much the peak exceeds a criterion.

Field.name: ModelFile
Field.usage: Model file with points or lines to be erased
Field.manpage: Input model file specifying points or lines to be erased.

Field.name: LineObjects
Field.usage: Objects that define lines to be replaced
Field.tooltip: List of objects that define lines to be replaced. Ranges can be entered, and / to specify all objects.
Field.manpage: List of objects that define lines to be replaced. Ranges can be entered, and / to specify all objects.

Field.name: BoundaryObjects
Field.usage: Objects that contain boundary contours around points to be replaced
Field.manpage: List of objects that contain boundary contours around pixels to be replaced. Ranges can be entered, and / to specify all objects. Boundary contours can be arbitrarily large. When a contour encloses more than 1000 pixels, a different procedure is use to erase the points, and intensities are tapered down over 8 pixels on the inside of the patch from the value of the nearest pixel just outside the patch to the mean of the surrounding pixels.

Field.name: AllSectionObjects
Field.usage: Objects with points to be replaced on all sections
Field.tooltip: List of objects with points to be replaced on all sections. Ranges can be entered, and / to specify all objects.
Field.manpage: List of objects with points to be replaced on all sections. Ranges can be entered, and / to specify all objects.

Field.name: CircleObjects
Field.usage: Objects with scattered points for replacing pixels within a circle
Field.manpage: List of objects that contain scattered points for replacing pixels within a circle around each point. The sphere radius, which can be an individual value for each point, is used to indicate the size of circle to replace. Ranges can be entered, and / to specify all objects.

Field.name: BetterRadius
Field.usage: Radii to use in place of defaults for points with no individual size
Field.manpage: For circle objects, this entry specifies a radius to use for points without an individual point size instead of the object's default sphere radius. This entry is floating point and can be used to overcome the limitations of having an integer default sphere radius. If there are multiple circle objects, enter one value to apply to all objects or a value for each object.

Field.name: ExpandCircleIterations
Field.usage: Number of iterations for expanding patches around circles
Field.manpage: Number of iterations of a procedure that expands the area erased around the points of a circle object. This procedure analyzes the intensity of pixels adjacent to the patch being erased and adds pixels in the appropriate tail of the intensity distribution to the patch. Iterating simply repeats the procedure. If edges of gold particles are left because points are not very well centered, try this option instead of just increasing the radius, as it will tend to erase just the remaining points on the edge instead of a whole ring of points.

Field.name: IncludeHaloInExpand
Field.usage: Include extreme intensities of other polarity when expanding
Field.manpage: Include the most extreme intensities of the opposite polarity from the bead (e.g., brighter intensities when beads are dark) when expanding the patch. This option may give a minor reduction in the visible halo around a bead due to underfocus, and often makes the intensity in the erased region seem to match the background better.

Field.name: TargetRadiusForExpand
Field.usage: Do expand operation as if circles were reduced to this radius
Field.manpage: This option makes the expansion of patches in images with a small pixel size more effective in two ways: 1) The pixels to be added to the patch are detected in images smoothed with a real-space Gaussian kernel. The Gaussian sigma is chosen to produce about the same amount of averaging as scaling down images by the amount that would make the maximum radius to be erased equal to the entered value. In fact, the sigma is just the ratio of that maximum radius to the given value. 2) The number of iterations is multiplied by that sigma value so that a comparable fraction of the bead size can be expanded into as when the pixel size is larger. In addition, when filling with noise, the border region in which noise will be measured is expanded by the sigma value. The option has no effect if the maximum radius is not bigger than the entered value.

Field.name: MergePatches
Field.usage: Merge patches in model that touch each other
Field.tooltip: Merge patches in the model that touch each other, if the resulting patch is less than the maximum radius
Field.manpage: Merge patches in the model if they touch each other, as long as the resulting patch is still within the maximum radius. Patches from objects with points to be replaced on all sections are ignored. This option should be used if an output model from automatic peak finding is modified and used as an input model.

Field.name: SkipTurnedOffPoints
Field.usage: Skip points with values below threshold if they are turned off
Field.manpage: Skip points in the model with contour values below threshold if they are not visible in 3dmod, namely if "Turn off below threshold" is set in the Bead Fixer, or "Turn off Low" is set in the Values panel of the Model View Object Edit dialog.

Field.name: BorderSize
Field.usage: Size of border around points in patch (default %{default})
Field.tooltip: Size of border around points in patch, which contains the points which will be fit to (the default is 2 pixels).
Field.manpage: Size of border around points in patch, which contains the points which will be fit to (the default is %{default} pixels)

Field.name: PolynomialOrder
Field.usage: Order of polynomial to fit to border points (default %{default})
Field.tooltip: Order of polynomial to fit to border points (the default is 2, which includes terms in x, y, x**2, y**2 and x*y).
Field.manpage: Order of polynomial to fit to border points. The default is %{default}, which includes terms in x, y, x**2, y**2 and x*y. The order can be between -1 and 3, where 0 will simply replace the pixels with the mean of the border points instead of fitting to them, and -1 will fill the area with noise matching the standard deviation in surrounding pixels.

Field.name: ExcludeAdjacent
Field.usage: Exclude points adjacent to patch points from the fit
Field.manpage: Exclude points adjacent to patch points from the fit; in other words, compute the polynomial fit to points that do not touch the ones being replaced.

Field.name: TrialMode
Field.usage: Analyze without writing output file
Field.tooltip: Run ccderaser in trial mode creating a x-ray model which can be viewed in 3dmod. This will not create an output stack.
Field.manpage: Analyze for replacement points without writing output image file.
